 At Landis+Gyr, were helping shape the future of energy making it more intelligent, resilient, and sustainable. Trusted by more than 2,000 utilities worldwide, our intelligent solutions connect devices, data, and decisions across the grid, helping customers modernize infrastructure, optimize operations, and deliver energy that is more reliable, resilient, accessible, safe, and sustainable. Technical Implementation Manager The Technical Implementation Manager (TIM) owns the technical delivery of Landis+Gyrs AMI products and solutions for new customer deployments and upgrades. The role covers both containerized deployments on Kubernetes (GKE and RKE), delivered using CI/CD pipelines and automation, and multi-tier deployments of the Head-End System (HES) across Windows and Linux servers. Across both, the TIM takes the Landis+Gyr solution from environment readiness through to production, covering the full stack from head-end software to field network endpoints. Working closely with Program Managers, infrastructure teams, customer IT and operations teams, and Landis+Gyr engineering and product groups, the TIM is accountable for a successful go-live. This includes resolving technical issues that arise during deployment and the hypercare period, and transitioning the solution smoothly to the support organization. The role calls for deep hands-on DevOps expertise and a strong working knowledge of GCP, combined with the planning and customer-facing skills needed to deliver complex deployments on schedule. Deploy, configure and upgrade containerized applications on Kubernetes (GKE and RKE) using Docker and Helm charts. JOB DESCRIPTION Production Manager Modular Kitchens, Wardrobes & Wooden Doors Manufacturing Department: Production
 Designation: Production Manager
 Industry: Modular Kitchens, Wardrobes, Wooden Doors & Customized Furniture Manufacturing
 Reporting To: Director / Business Head
 Job Location: Factory / Manufacturing Unit 1. Job Summary The Production Manager will be responsible for managing the complete factory operations, including production planning, preparation of cutlists, material management, machine operations, workforce supervision, quality control and timely dispatch of finished products. The candidate must have practical knowledge of modular kitchens, wardrobes, wooden doors and customized furniture manufacturing processes. 2. Key Responsibilities A. Production Planning & Execution Prepare daily, weekly and monthly production plans as per project requirements and delivery schedules. Manage the complete production process for modular kitchens, wardrobes, wooden doors and customized furniture. Ensure timely completion of factory work as per approved drawings and project deadlines. Allocate jobs to operators, carpenters, machine operators and other factory staff. Monitor production progress and resolve manufacturing-related issues. B. Cutlist Preparation & Technical Drawings Prepare accurate cutlists for modular kitchens, wardrobes, cabinets and wooden doors based on approved drawings and measurements. Calculate panel sizes, carcass dimensions, shutter sizes, shelves, partitions, fillers and other components. Read and understand 2D/3D drawings, sectional drawings and production specifications. Prepare material requirements for plywood, HDHMR, MDF, Boilo boards, laminates, veneers and other materials. Coordinate with the design and drafting team to clarify drawing discrepancies before production. Ensure correct cutting dimensions, edge-banding details, drilling positions and hardware specifications. Minimize material wastage through proper cutting optimization and nesting. C. Factory & Machine Management Supervise panel saws, edge-banding machines, multiboring machines, CNC machines and other production equipment, as applicable. Ensure proper machine settings, safe operations and preventive maintenance. Monitor the workflow from material cutting to edge banding, drilling, assembly, finishing and packing. Coordinate PU painting and finishing activities wherever applicable. Maintain production discipline and ensure efficient utilization of machinery and manpower. D. Material & Inventory Management Check raw material availability before starting production. Coordinate with the purchase and store departments for timely material procurement. Monitor the consumption of boards, laminates, veneers, adhesives, hardware and other consumables. Maintain records of material issued, material consumed, wastage and balance stock. Control unnecessary material usage and reduce production costs. E. Quality Control Inspect components at cutting, edge-banding, drilling, assembly and finishing stages. Ensure dimensions and finishes match approved drawings, samples and specifications. Check shutter alignment, edge quality, hardware fitting, surface finish and overall workmanship. Identify manufacturing defects and implement corrective actions. Ensure finished products are properly inspected before packing and dispatch. F. Manpower & Factory Administration Manage and supervise factory workers, machine operators, carpenters, assemblers and finishing staff. Allocate responsibilities and monitor employee productivity. Maintain attendance, shift schedules, production records and daily work reports. Train employees in quality standards, machine safety and efficient working methods. Maintain discipline, housekeeping and safety standards throughout the factory. G. Project Coordination & Dispatch Coordinate with project managers, site supervisors, designers, purchase, stores and dispatch teams. Prioritize production according to site requirements and project deadlines. Ensure all components are properly labelled, packed and dispatched with the required hardware and accessories. Handle urgent project requirements and resolve production delays. Support site teams in resolving manufacturing, fitting and measurement-related issues. 3. Daily Reporting Requirements The Production Manager must prepare and submit daily reports covering: Production completed against the planned target. Project-wise production status for kitchens, wardrobes and doors. Cutlists prepared and jobs released for manufacturing. Raw material consumption and wastage. Machine breakdowns and production downtime. Quality issues, rejected components and rework. Manpower attendance and productivity. Pending jobs, dispatch status and next-day production planning. 4. Required Skills & Qualifications Diploma, ITI or degree in Mechanical Engineering, Production, Furniture Technology or a related field preferred. Relevant experience in modular kitchen, wardrobe, wooden door or furniture manufacturing. Strong practical knowledge of cutlist preparation and board optimization. Ability to read technical drawings and understand manufacturing dimensions. Knowledge of plywood, HDHMR, MDF, laminates, veneers, hardware and furniture fittings. Experience with factory machinery and production workflow. Working knowledge of Excel and production reporting; CAD or furniture-design software knowledge preferred. Strong leadership, planning, coordination and problem-solving skills. 5. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) The performance of the Production Manager will be evaluated on: Timely completion of production schedules. Accuracy of cutlists and manufacturing dimensions. Reduction in raw material wastage. Quality of finished products and reduction in rework. Machine utilization and workforce productivity. Control over production costs and material consumption.  Key Responsibilities 1. CSR Communications & Impact Storytelling Develop and execute internal and external CSR communication plans and calendars. Identify and develop compelling CSR impact stories, employee stories, beneficiary stories and project highlights. Draft CSR communications including employee mailers, campaign content, leadership updates, newsletters, social media content and other communication collateral. Work with internal communications and relevant stakeholders to amplify CSR initiatives across appropriate channels. Coordinate with NGO partners to source project updates, photographs, testimonials and impact data for storytelling. Ensure CSR communications are accurate, consistent, engaging and aligned with company communication and brand guidelines. Support communications around volunteering, giving campaigns and key CSR milestones. 2. Develop campaign concepts, messaging, launch plans and employee engagement strategies. Partner with relevant teams and stakeholders to increase awareness and participation. Integrate giving and volunteering opportunities wherever relevant to create stronger employee engagement around social causes. Track participation, campaign performance and giving trends, and recommend actions to improve engagement. Support campaign governance, NGO due diligence, approvals, launch and closure documentation. 3. CSR Project Management, Monitoring & Evaluation Manage assigned CSR projects and relationships with NGO/implementation partners. Coordinate project plans, milestones, deliverables, budgets, KPIs and reporting requirements with partners. Conduct regular project review and monitoring meetings with NGOs. Review project progress against agreed objectives, targets and timelines. Validate program data, beneficiary outcomes, utilization and supporting documentation. Identify delivery gaps, risks and delays and coordinate appropriate corrective actions. Support periodic project assessments, site visits and partner performance reviews. Experience Relevant experience in one or more of the following: Corporate Social Responsibility / ESG / Social Impact; Corporate or internal communications; Employee engagement or giving programs; NGO/development-sector project management; Program monitoring and evaluation. Experience working with NGO/community partners would be preferred. Exposure to employee giving, volunteering or social-impact platforms would be an advantage.
